groups.reasoning: ReadResult shared body interprets success JSON or null outcome-unknown; error body parse failure falls back status message, >=500 unknown. Same known/unknown outcome policy for financial idempotent commands; malformed success is unknown, not proof rollback. Both share common Application request/response types where imported; local generic result/error wrappers remain separate.

Login bodies equal: obtain server-issued token, set HttpClient default Authorization and return projected current-user fields. Successful login mutates shared ApiClient auth before view-model followup. UI020 context remains qualified prior finding; helper equality is not proof identical callers or permissions. PIN values never captured or executed.

SendAsync shared body disposes HTTP response, maps HTTP/cancellation/JSON/IO exceptions to financial outcome unknown and same-key retry wording. Does not itself retain/retry requests or ensure idempotency; server journal and calling view model do that. Cashier separate ReadAsync changes message for reads, CallCenter uses SendAsync more broadly.

Both WinUI image-URI helpers return null for missing version/base address; otherwise escape ID/version into same route. Cashier comments differ only. No financial amount calculated; generic gateway duplication only, preexisting image authentication candidate remains paused, not validated by this comparison.

Logout bodies equal: attempt server revoke, swallow failure then clear local token/header. Local end does not prove remote invalidation on network failure; server expiry separate. No cross-client singleton/session sharing proven.

Three string-base constructors (legacy WPF, CashierWinUI, CallCenter) construct HttpClient with same default localhost5151 and10second timeout. Injected-HttpClient overload/configuration can differ, so identical constructor body does not prove identical deployed host/session/lifetime. No runtime connection initiated.
CreatePrintJobs wrappers equal route-escaped order ID/body/result. Queue request separate from financial success; no paper sent. This is narrow API mirror classification, not resumed printing audit.

Both WinUI PingHealth dispose response and return HTTP success, catch all including cancellation as false. It tests endpoint reachability/status, not DB/payment readiness. Legacy WPF health response lacks using and is not in this exact-body group; do not infer identical lifetime across legacy.
GetSettings identical wrapper delegates to SendAsync and common Application SettingsDto; no local settings/database mutation. Transport failure classification shared even though read-only request.
OpenShift wrappers equal route/request type. Neither calculates opening cash or enforces balance/permission locally; server OpenShift handler owns FIN011 lock issue.

PrepareShiftClose wrappers equal request/route and nullable result handling. Read-only preview represented POST; not actual close or movement. Same transport unknown classification does not post money itself.
CloseShift wrappers equal shared DTO and endpoint. Client body equality does not supply server concurrency/reconciliation or validated approval provenance; FIN017 authoritative server issue retained.

Checkout wrappers equal shared request/route/result; prices, fees, stock and totals resolved server-side. No client cash/callcenter alternate formula in these bodies. FIN016 server signed-fee boundary cannot be repaired merely by merging wrappers.
Refund wrappers equal shared DTO/route. Shared HTTP method does not establish same caller role, original/current shift attribution or refund eligibility; server FIN003/004 semantics independent.
Electronic-confirm wrappers equal common request/result and route. No payment-leg arithmetic in client wrapper; server FIN001 mixed-idempotency issue survives both clients.
Cancel-pending wrappers equal common request/result and route. Server FIN002 cancellation-versus-collected split cash concern is not a differing client formula.

IssueManagerApproval wrappers equal body/endpoint. Requests are server authority, not client-generated manager proof. Same client methods present does not mean CallCenter role may execute every financial API.
Expense wrappers equal route/common DTO. Server chooses real source account permission and validates amounts; no duplicated expense calculation here.
SafeDrop wrappers equal body/result/route; server owns drawer/account/shift authorization and transaction. Wrapper does not guard current shift status or overdraw independently.
Cashier cash movement wrappers equal DTO/route; server movement type/account logic remains one authoritative implementation.
Cash-drawer-open wrappers equal shared request/route. This comparison invoked no API/hardware; no physical drawer or print operation performed.
Nested sender lambda within CreatePrintJobs identical. Captures its own HttpClient/order/request/ct; no shared instance or financial ledger effect inferred from token equality.

independently_source_read_not_new_functi: These callable IDs already have UI-review receipts; no original financial or global function count increment claimed.

divergent_near_mirrors.difference: CallCenter uses SendAsync read failure monetary retry wording; Cashier uses ReadAsync non-monetary message. Both have unknown flag true on transport failure. No financial write from GET.
Same server balance contract, SendAsync vs ReadAsync affects message; no client balance formula.

limits: No HTTP/auth/DB/native operations. Generic image/print glue classified without reopening paused security-image/printing investigations. Other mirrored code outside these groups not complete.
